text:
olga: Heads-up — observed three distinct preemptible eviction waves in us-west1 spot-gpu pool between 09:03 and 09:22. ~18 nodes terminated total, many pods went Running->Pending quickly because CA couldn't find replacement quota.
infra-bot: alert: spot-eviction | region=us-west1 | node_count=18 | window=19m
kevin: ouch. any pattern on instance types or node labels?
olga: mostly nvidia-a100-80gb-ish families + a few v100s. eviction timestamps clustered by AZ (us-west1-a then -c). CA logs show failures: "no capacity" on request despite quota available in project — looks like cloud provider couldn't satisfy specific SKU mix.
maria: CA config? are we using balanced or least-waste expander? also what's the fallback pool configured as? alex: we use cluster-autoscaler with expander: "least-waste" for gpu pools, and an overflow node group (preemptible-fallback-2) with mixed instance types but it's very small (min=2).
kevin: if provider returns SKU mismatch, mixed instance groups don't help unless you allow cross-family. Could we enable launchTemplate with multiple instance types per nodegroup (and increase group min temporarily)?
olga: short-term mitigation I pushed: increased preemptible-fallback-2 min from 2 -> 6 and bumped surge to allow faster joins. It reduced pending backlog but cost will spike.
sam: cost spike ok short-term — we've SLA on demo infra. But we should avoid manual fiddles. propose: 1) prewarm small GPU micro-pool in each region (eg 4x tiny-GPU nodes) that are always kept warm and pinned to a subset of lightweight model loads; 2) autoscaler topology-awareness: allow CA to launch in any compatible family; 3) improve eviction smoothing so we don't cordon/drain aggressively when multiple AZs evict.
maria: +1 for prewarm pools. also we should use node-level preemption hooks: set eviction handler to persist KV cache to S3 quickly so warmup is faster on replacement.
alex: experiment idea: maintain a tiny fleet of cpu-only "adapter" nodes with model shard prefetcher service that can quickly serve inference at lower perf during GPU shortfall. avoids total outage while we spin GPUs back up.
kevin: that needs product buy-in but sounds viable as a graded-degradation strategy.
olga: longer term infra changes I recommend:
- increase mixed-gpu-nodegroup diversity (allow more families in one ASG)
- set CA flags: --balance-similar-node-groups=false, --skip nodes-with-system-pods=false (careful), tune --max-node-provision-time to 5m
- implement regional prewarm pool (min 4) per region tagged "spot-prewarm" and a fast priority routing rule that sends low-QPS fallback traffic there
- add quota reservations for fallback capacity in critical regions

kevin: config snippet for bumping CA max provision time and expander change:
```
# patch deployment cluster-autoscaler
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment cluster-autoscaler --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"cluster-autoscaler","args":["--expander=least-waste","--max-node-provision-time=5m"]}]}}}}'
```
maria: We'll also need to update our autoscaler IAM role to allow trying more instance types per request; cloud provider sometimes rejects if role doesn't allow specifying alternatives.
infra-bot: note: created incident ticket INF-4721 for "us-west1 spot eviction wave" and cron job to collect CA logs during next 24h.
olga: quick checklist for on-call if this reoccurs:
- check infra-bot alerts + CA events (kubectl get events -n kube-system)
- inspect cloud provider "capacityErrors" in provider logs
- temporarily increase fallback pool min size and let CA settle
- if capacity errors persist, open provider support case and consider region-failover

sam: can we schedule a short chaos test for next sprint that simulates AZ-specific spot evictions so we validate prewarm+fallback flows?
kevin: yes, add a controlled chaos job (kill nodes by label) and measure tail latency + pending count. target: <30s tail for fallback route.
olga: assigning follow-ups: kevin -> run diversity experiment (allow cross-family), maria -> design prewarm pool + cache persist handler, alex -> prototype cpu-adapter fallback. I'll own the incident ticket and cost impact notes.
maria: created RFC draft: /docs/rfcs/prewarm-and-fallback.md (WIP) — pinged product for cost tradeoffs.
kevin: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to review experiment plan. :thumbsup:
alex: ack
infra-bot: incident INF-4721 status: acknowledged by olga\n
